summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, with EBIT margin exiting near 10% versus 6.8% in H1.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, led by 10% growth in ECD and 14% growth in lighting. Management said EBIT margin improved from 6.8% in H1 to about 10% in Q4, driven by operating leverage, premiumisation, pricing and cost optimisation. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 271 Cr (11.9% margin). Butterfly returned to double-digit revenue and profit growth, and management took an impairment on its Butterfly carrying value, which is non-cash but hits ROCE and asset turnover. Management also announced a new super-premium product line, Crompton Rhion, and an identical dividend to last year.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, Q4; management called it industry-leading
YoY, Q4, with steady EBIT margins
Management says Butterfly is now cash flow positive

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 10%, broad-based across pumps, small domestic appliances and fans. Fans saw record March volumes; BLDC portfolio growing 30%-plus. Management says it gained share in every ECD product in FY26 but did not give category numbers.

segments.name: Small domestic appliances (SDA)
segments.commentary: Management said FY26 growth was in the early 20s percent and Q4 growth close to 30%, with a step-up in profitability. New launches included infrared cooktops, air fryers and premium juicers.

segments.name: Lighting (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 14%. Government share of B2B mix fell about 500 bps in FY26. Y-o-Y margin said to be roughly flat despite materially higher ad spend in the quarter.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 17% with steady EBIT margins and higher advertising spend. Management says it is back to strong double-digit growth in both revenue and profit, and an impairment was taken on its carrying value.

segments.name: Solar pumps and rooftop (new PLs)
segments.commentary: Solar pumps revenue was about Rs 200 Cr last year and grew significantly this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr (about 38,000 units in Andhra plus Telangana), with about 5,000 homes installed so far. Management targets a Rs 2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years (corrected from Rs 1,500 Cr).

segments.name: Wires (Crompton Armor)
segments.commentary: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and now selling in South India; national rollout is planned over the year rather than all at once.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margins to recover over time as input-cost turbulence from the war eases, but would not give a timeline.
Management said further material cost inflation came in April; it plans to offset this through pricing and Unnati cost actions, and says some benefits could be back-ended.
Dividend declared identical to last year.
Solar business aspiration: Rs 2,000 Cr over 3-4 years (management corrected the figure from Rs 1,500 Cr).
Butterfly will focus on gaining traction in North, East, West (NEW) markets in the coming year.
Water heater BEE norms from July: management said it is fully prepared, with some cost increase to mitigate or pass on.
capex_capacity: Annual R&D and innovation spend about Rs 100 Cr, per management.
Rhion super-premium PL created; the Large Kitchen Appliance business folds into it; about 70 EBOs already operating.
Lighting supply chain restructured: Baddi unit restructured earlier, Baroda cost base reset with VRS.
Wires rollout ramping from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to other states over the year.
Solar rooftop execution stepped up in the last 2-3 months.
demand_pricing: Two price increases in ECD since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative price increase in fans in FY26, mostly taken in Q4.
Management said cost inflation continued into April; a war room tracks costs weekly or daily.
Butterfly has taken price increases similar to ECD's.
Residential pumps demand was tepid due to heavy rain; management says it held share. Agricultural pumps grew in the teens after product launches.
Air cooler inventory was cleared in the season; management says it gained marginal share. Water heaters were among the top 2 players in GT, now said to be No. 2.
Management says traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY and solar pump collections are on expectation; no stress seen so far in builders or contractors.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases were taken against the cost inflation, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Two ECD price increases since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative in fans in FY26, mostly in Q4, which offset material inflation. Further inflation came in April, and management is waiting to see before deciding pricing for the rest of Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 contribution and FY27 ramp-up from solar pumps and rooftops?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar pumps grew from about Rs 20 Cr three years ago to about Rs 200 Cr last year, and grew strongly again this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr, with about 5,000 homes installed. Management declined to give an FY27 contribution estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins dip, and is growth troughing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins were roughly flat YoY despite higher ad spend. Growth came from a shift away from government B2B contracts (down about 500 bps), a higher-ASP B2C mix (panels, floodlights) and a reset supply chain and cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Butterfly impairment's tax impact and is the merger still planned?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tax angle and it is an accounting impairment, not a write-off. Management said the impairment is unrelated to the merger plan, which remains on the cards at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the national rollout plan for wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, with ramp-up across the country over the year and distribution via the full Crompton network. No specific revenue targets given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there channel or payment stress in the value chain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY, solar pump collections are on track, and FY26 operating cash flow crossed Rs 500 Cr. Management said builder and contractor exposure is small and no stress is seen so far.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from the war and fresh April increases; margin recovery depends on pass-through and whether competitors follow on pricing.
Butterfly impairment hits ROCE and asset turnover; watch Butterfly growth in NEW markets outside the South.
Water heater BEE norms from July may add cost and pressure margins in LDA.
Solar rooftop order book execution (about 38,000 units in Andhra and Telangana) and collections from government-linked solar pump contractors.
No ECD category breakdown or new-segment revenue disclosure, so growth contribution is hard to verify.
Rhion go-to-market and sourcing details still undisclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, margin recovery and growth momentum in lighting, SDA and Butterfly. Cautious on near-term input costs and war-driven inflation, and evasive on segment-level splits, solar revenue targets and Rhion sourcing, which were deferred to offline discussions.
key_quotes: So, this is a quarter where we've been very focused on margin discipline. Our EBIT margins improved from 6.8% in H1 to exit at about 10% in Q4.
Butterfly business delivered a 17% revenue growth together with steady EBIT margins.

adds.what: Crompton Armor wires national rollout from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to other states over the year

growth.why: Q4 revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr with ECD +10%, lighting +14%, Butterfly +17%, and Q4 SDA near 30%; the solar ambition of Rs 2,000 Cr in 3-4 years is backed only by a Rs 500 Cr rooftop order book and a Rs 200 Cr base, with no capacity figures, and margin recovery has no timeline.
